name: What makes an ADU kitchen feel more spacious during design review?

mainEntity.name: How can a contractor make a small ADU kitchen look and function larger on the plans?
mainEntity.text: How can a contractor make a small ADU kitchen look and function larger on the plans?

acceptedAnswer.text: A small ADU kitchen can be made to feel larger on the drawings and in real life by reducing visual clutter and keeping the layout efficient. Long uninterrupted counter runs, compact appliances, and restrained cabinetry help the room read as simpler and more open. Designers often improve the feeling of space by aligning cabinet depths, minimizing awkward corners, and placing the sink where the room has the best natural light. Even on a permit set, the kitchen should communicate ease of movement and practical function. This matters because many homeowners make decisions based on how the kitchen looks on paper before they ever see it built. The best layouts are usually the ones that appear calm and logical rather than overdesigned. In ADU construction, spaciousness is often created through proportion and planning, not square footage. A good contractor will use the kitchen plan to solve multiple goals at once: function, permitting, cost control, and visual openness.
acceptedAnswer.description: A small ADU kitchen feels more spacious when the plan uses simple lines, efficient storage, compact appliances, and clear circulation. Design choices like one continuous counter run, fewer visual breaks, and light finishes make the kitchen read larger before it is even built.
